Norm: The Rule for Measuring Length

How do we measure the length of a vector? The measuring rule is the norm.

The rule has three parts. A length is never negative, and only the zero vector has length 0. Scaling a vector scales its length by the same factor. And the length of a sum never exceeds the sum of the lengths. That last rule is the triangle inequality. Change the ruler and the length changes: the block-counting ruler, the straight-line ruler, and the king-move ruler all differ.

For example, in a 🏙 grid city, go one block east and one block north. The straight line is one diagonal, but on blocks you must walk twice. A chess king goes diagonally in one move. The same move measures 2, about 1.41, and 1 under the three rulers.

Examples & Exercises

For the vector \x = (3, 4)\, compute \\\|x\\|_1\, \\\|x\\|_2\, and \\\|x\\|_\\infty\ each.

∥x∥1=∣x1∣+∣x2∣,∥x∥2=x12+x22,∥x∥∞=max⁡(∣x1∣,∣x2∣)\|x\|_1 = |x_1| + |x_2|, \qquad \|x\|_2 = \sqrt{x_1^2 + x_2^2}, \qquad \|x\|_\infty = \max(|x_1|, |x_2|)∥x∥1​=∣x1​∣+∣x2​∣,∥x∥2​=x12​+x22​​,∥x∥∞​=max(∣x1​∣,∣x2​∣)
Show proof

  1. ∥x∥1=∣3∣+∣4∣=7\|x\|_1 = |3| + |4| = 7∥x∥1​=∣3∣+∣4∣=7.

  2. ∥x∥2=32+42=25=5\|x\|_2 = \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{25} = 5∥x∥2​=32+42​=25​=5.

  3. ∥x∥∞=max⁡(∣3∣,∣4∣)=4\|x\|_\infty = \max(|3|, |4|) = 4∥x∥∞​=max(∣3∣,∣4∣)=4. The same vector measures 7, 5, and 4 under the three rulers.

Prove completely, from the norm axioms, the reverse triangle inequality ∣∥x∥−∥y∥∣≤∥x−y∥|\|x\| - \|y\|| \le \|x - y\|∣∥x∥−∥y∥∣≤∥x−y∥.

∣∥x∥−∥y∥∣≤∥x−y∥|\|x\| - \|y\|| \le \|x - y\|∣∥x∥−∥y∥∣≤∥x−y∥
Show proof

  1. Since x=(x−y)+yx = (x - y) + yx=(x−y)+y, the triangle inequality gives ∥x∥≤∥x−y∥+∥y∥\|x\| \le \|x - y\| + \|y\|∥x∥≤∥x−y∥+∥y∥. Rearranging, ∥x∥−∥y∥≤∥x−y∥\|x\| - \|y\| \le \|x - y\|∥x∥−∥y∥≤∥x−y∥.

  2. Swapping the roles of xxx and yyy gives ∥y∥−∥x∥≤∥y−x∥\|y\| - \|x\| \le \|y - x\|∥y∥−∥x∥≤∥y−x∥. But ∥y−x∥=∥(−1)(x−y)∥=∥x−y∥\|y - x\| = \|(-1)(x - y)\| = \|x - y\|∥y−x∥=∥(−1)(x−y)∥=∥x−y∥, so ∥y∥−∥x∥≤∥x−y∥\|y\| - \|x\| \le \|x - y\|∥y∥−∥x∥≤∥x−y∥ holds too.

  3. Combining the two inequalities, ∣∥x∥−∥y∥∣=max⁡(∥x∥−∥y∥,∥y∥−∥x∥)≤∥x−y∥|\|x\| - \|y\|| = \max(\|x\| - \|y\|, \|y\| - \|x\|) \le \|x - y\|∣∥x∥−∥y∥∣=max(∥x∥−∥y∥,∥y∥−∥x∥)≤∥x−y∥. This is the reverse triangle inequality.

On a vector space with a norm ∥⋅∥\|\cdot\|∥⋅∥, put d(x,y)=∥x−y∥d(x, y) = \|x - y\|d(x,y)=∥x−y∥. Prove completely that ddd satisfies all the metric axioms.

d(x,y)=∥x−y∥d(x, y) = \|x - y\|d(x,y)=∥x−y∥
Show proof

  1. Non-negativity and separation: by the first norm axiom, d(x,y)=∥x−y∥≥0d(x, y) = \|x - y\| \ge 0d(x,y)=∥x−y∥≥0, and d(x,y)=0d(x, y) = 0d(x,y)=0 is equivalent to ∥x−y∥=0\|x - y\| = 0∥x−y∥=0, which is equivalent to x−y=0x - y = 0x−y=0, that is, x=yx = yx=y.

  2. Symmetry: by the second norm axiom, d(y,x)=∥y−x∥=∥(−1)(x−y)∥=∣−1∣∥x−y∥=∥x−y∥=d(x,y)d(y, x) = \|y - x\| = \|(-1)(x - y)\| = |-1| \|x - y\| = \|x - y\| = d(x, y)d(y,x)=∥y−x∥=∥(−1)(x−y)∥=∣−1∣∥x−y∥=∥x−y∥=d(x,y).

  3. Triangle inequality: by the third norm axiom, d(x,z)=∥x−z∥=∥(x−y)+(y−z)∥≤∥x−y∥+∥y−z∥=d(x,y)+d(y,z)d(x, z) = \|x - z\| = \|(x - y) + (y - z)\| \le \|x - y\| + \|y - z\| = d(x, y) + d(y, z)d(x,z)=∥x−z∥=∥(x−y)+(y−z)∥≤∥x−y∥+∥y−z∥=d(x,y)+d(y,z). All four axioms hold, so ddd is a metric.
